Off the back of this, I've noticed that setting sleep start also changes sleep end. I plan on addressing this in a separate PR.
It also seems like Starlink isn't happy when end time is very close behind start time (ex. start time 3PM, end time 2PM). I'm still trying to figure out if this is a real limitation with Starlink, and if it is how we can communicate that to users in homeassistant. This can also be done in a separate PR

review_comments: We shouldn't try to do datetime math ourselves as its very hard to get it right. Use datetime objects and than convert back the `total_seconds` when done

I mentioned it in another comment above, but I'm fairly sure we are dealing with "seconds since 00:00" in this case.
If that is indeed the case, using datetime objects will actually cause issues, especially around daylight savings.
If that's not the case, I'm happy to change this :slightly_smiling_face:

From the doc string it looks like everything is in UTC so you should be able to use UTC time which doesn't have timezone or DST concerns

https://github.com/sparky8512/starlink-grpc-tools/blob/37aeed63defcc9a8c3f52c9d8c7607988fede1c5/starlink_grpc.py#L1615

Apologies for the delay, I was working up the courage to fight Python again 😅
I've been poking around in docs, and it doesn't look like we can actually add/subtract `datetime.time` instances from each other. Were you proposing that we concern ourselves with dates here? That seems redundant.

It's a bit convoluted that it gets converted in `_time_to_utc_minutes` and then converted again in `async_set_sleep_duration` function.  It would be nicer to convert it once, but you have another function in that case, so on second thought, I think this is fine.

Subtracting 24 hours does not account for incrementing the day.
Also, could it be more than 1 day?

> Subtracting 24 hours does not account for incrementing the day.

In true datetime arithmetic, that'd be true. We aren't doing true datetime arithmetic though, so I don't expect it to be a problem

>  Also, could it be more than 1 day?

Answered below.
The value of "duration" could still be negative if multiple days are possible. Is it possible to be more than 1 day?
As far as I'm aware, multiple days are not possible.
